chapter_title: From the Diary of Anne Frank & Amanda!

branches.theme: Prose Excerpts: From the Diary of Anne Frank

details: 13-year-old Anne Frank feels that despite having a loving family, sister Margot, and 30 acquaintances, she lacks a true confidant.
She asserts 'paper has more patience than people', believing a diary absorbs deep feelings silently without judgment.
She names her diary 'Kitty' to treat it as an intimate friend.
evidence_or_examples: Anne's quote: 'Paper has more patience than people.'

details: Anne describes her class waiting nervously for exam results.
Her math teacher Mr. Keesing is annoyed by her perpetual talking during class.
He assigns extra homework essays: 1) 'A Chatterbox' 2) 'An Incorrigible Chatterbox' 3) 'Quack, Quack, Quack, Said Mistress Chatterbox'.
evidence_or_examples: Anne arguing in essay 1 that talking is a student trait inherited from her mother.

details: For the third essay, Anne enlists her friend Sanne to help write a poem.
The poem tells of a father swan who bites his three ducklings to death because they quack too much.
Mr. Keesing takes the satirical joke in good humor, reads the poem to the class, and permits Anne to speak without further punishment.
evidence_or_examples: Keesing laughing at the duckling poem and quoting it to other classes.

branches.theme: Poetic Study: Amanda! by Robin Klein

sub_branches.concept: Parental Control vs Adolescent Mental Escapism
details: Direct stanzas feature a parent nagging Amanda about biting nails, hunching shoulders, eating chocolate, cleaning shoes, and finishing homework.

Parenthetical stanzas represent Amanda's silent mental withdrawal into daydreams of absolute solitude: 1) A sole green mermaid drifting peacefully in sea 2) An orphan roaming barefoot making dusty street patterns 3) Rapunzel living a tranquil, undisturbed life in a high tower.
evidence_or_examples: Parenthetical line: '(There is a languid, emerald sea, / where the sole inhabitant is me— / a mermaid, drifting blissfully.)'
